correctness.rationale: The exact unnormalized Fourier eigenvalue is derived by character-shell summation and the identity ∑K_j=0 off the trivial character. For q/n→c the proof gives a uniform finite-codimension cutoff with all K_1,K_2,K_3 nonnegative outside it; fixed-codimension K_3/n³ converges to the stated polynomial, so spectral upper and lower sandwiches yield the limit. A discriminant factorization proves the sharp c=1/2 switch, and a strict limiting codimension gap plus the positive derivative of the full-weight eigenvalue proves exact alphabet-independent endpoint stabilization below that ratio. Fixed alphabet uses uniform cubic K_3/n³ convergence; fixed dimension uses leading q³ and q² coefficient comparisons, including the unique critical k=n-2 layer. Direct group-character enumerations and asymptotic checks passed in the packaged Python script; they do not substitute for the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Brouwer et al. analyze single distance-shell adjacency eigenvalues and determine the large-alphabet minimum of degree-three Krawtchouk values at fixed dimension, but the powered capped distance mixes K_1,K_2,K_3 with distinct exponent-dependent coefficients. Their theorem alone does not give the logarithmic constant (n-2)log(4/3)-log 2, nor the discrete-cubic minimum and its sharp c=1/2 switch. The published degree-two projection result concerns operator endpoint norms and a different quadratic Charlier law, not a third-degree powered-distance negativity threshold.

value.rationale: The four-cap metric has a motivated Hilbert-embedding/negative-type invariant. Its sharp alphabet/dimension threshold c=1/2, discrete critical-mode transition, and different fixed-dimension quadratic decay give a structural phase diagram not obtainable by merely renaming the Boolean cap-four or nonbinary cap-three cases. Explicit constants and multiplicity identify precise Fourier obstructions useful in studying snowflake embeddings and translation-invariant Gaussian kernels.
